app.title: Lamplight Nook
app.tagline: A cozy pixel shop where a small team does computer jobs for you with Claude.

nook.outside: changes something outside this commission's folder, which can be undone

startFail.text:
The disk may be full, or the data folder may not be writable. Free up some space and try again.

templates.label: Pick one, or just write
templates.pageFill: Make me a small web page that ...
templates.researchFill: Look into ... and write me a short summary.
templates.tidyFill: How should I tidy up this folder? ...
templates.albumFill: Make a little album of these photos: ...
templates.travelFill: Make me a travel guide for ..., ... days.
templates.toolFill: Make me a small tool that ...
templates.documentFill: Write me a Word document about ...
templates.slidesFill: Make me slides about ..., about ... slides.
templates.resumeHint: Hand over an old résumé or a list of what you've done, if you have one. Nothing gets made up; gaps are left for you to fill in.
templates.notesHint: Hand over your highlights and jottings. Quotations come only from what you hand over.
templates.toolHint: If it can work in a browser, it becomes a web page. A script only when files on your computer must change, and it only lists what it would do until you run it with -Apply.
templates.albumHint: Hand over the photos: drag them onto this slip, or use "Hand over files". The album is a web page made from copies.
templates.needPhotos: Hand over a few photos first, so the album has something in it.
templates.editHint: Only a copy is edited; your file stays as it is. Text, web pages, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF, up to 20 MB. A PDF comes back as a Word document.
templates.tidyHint: The staff only see names, sizes and dates. They write you a plan and move nothing.
templates.needSource: Choose the file or folder first.
templates.tooBig: That file is too big (over 20 MB). Try a smaller one.
templates.macros: That file carries macros, which would run when the changed copy is opened, so the shop won't take it. Save it without macros (as .docx, .xlsx or .pptx) and pick it again.

furnish.hint: This room: {scene}. Each room keeps its own colours, and what the shop has gathered stays put.

materials.label: Handed over
materials.hint: Screenshots, spreadsheets, drafts: anything helps. You can also drag files onto this slip or the counter. The staff work from copies; your files stay as they are.
materials.folder: “{name}” is a folder. To sort out a folder, use “Tidy a folder” above.
materials.tooBig: “{name}” is too big (20 MB each, 50 MB in all).
materials.tooMany: Ten files at most; “{name}” will have to wait.
materials.busy: The shop is busy with this one. Hand it over when it's done.
materials.drop: Let go to hand it to Wick

lent.pick: Work in a folder I already have…
lent.picked: The staff will change the files in this folder itself. Before a file is first changed, a copy of it is kept as it was, so you can undo the whole commission.
lent.broad: That's too much to hand over. The staff don't work across a whole drive, your home folder, Documents, Desktop or Downloads; pick a smaller folder inside.
lent.tooBig: That folder is too big (over 100 MB). The shop has to be able to keep a copy of everything in it before it can promise an undo. Try a smaller one.
lent.confirmText: The staff will change the files already in this folder without asking about each one. Before any file is first changed, the shop keeps a copy of it as it was.
lent.confirmUndo: If you don't like the result, press “Undo this commission” on the result card: changed files go back as they were, new ones are taken away, and nothing else is touched. Deleting files and running commands still ask you first.
lent.undoAsk: Undoing puts your changed files back as they were and takes away the new ones. What this commission made will be gone.
lent.undone: Undone. The folder is as it was before the work started.
lent.undoPartly: Undone, except for these: {files}. Their folder now leads somewhere outside, and the shop won't write there.
lent.undoFailed: Couldn't undo it; it may have been undone already.

ui.wantMissing: Write a line about what you'd like first.
ui.detailsPlaceholder: e.g. works on a phone too, large text
ui.budgetCap: This round spends at most {cap}; the staff stop and ask before going over. Change it in Settings.
ui.budgetNoCap: This round has no spending cap. You can set one in Settings.
ui.budgetLeft: {left} left this month, of the {cap} monthly limit.

consult.open: Talk it over with Wick first…
consult.title: Talking it over with Wick
consult.hello: What would you like made? Take your time: what it is, who it's for, what you have to go on, and how it should look.
consult.writing: Wick is writing up the slip…
consult.finish: That's it, write up the slip
consult.limits: A talk costs at most {cap}, and you can say up to {n} things.
consult.cap: Let's write the slip now. I've noted everything we said.
consult.trouble: I lost the thread just now. Let's write the slip; I've noted everything we said.
consult.filled: Wick wrote the slip from your talk. Look it over before you hand it in.
consult.filledChat: Your talk went into "Anything particular?". Look it over and tidy it before you hand it in.

ui.demoFill: Make me a little expense tracker page where I can note what I spend each day.
ui.resultBudgetMonth: Just so you know: about {spent} spent this month, of the {cap} monthly limit. {left} left.
ui.resultBudgetProject: Just so you know: "{project}" has cost about {spent}, of its {cap} limit. {left} left.
ui.statsLine: wrote files {writes} times, ran things {runs} times, {fails} failed

board.title: The plan on the blackboard
board.count: {done} of {total} done. Wick wrote this list and may change it along the way.

setup.welcomeText: I'm Wick, I run this shop. What should we call you?
setup.welcomeLook: And pick how you look when you drop by:
setup.claudeMissing: Claude Code isn't installed yet. The staff need it to work. It takes about two minutes, once.
setup.claudeStep1: Open PowerShell: press Start, type PowerShell, press Enter.
setup.claudeStep2: Paste this line and press Enter:
setup.claudeStep3: Then come back. The shop notices by itself, no restart needed.
setup.claudeWatching: Waiting for it to finish installing...
setup.claudeInstallHint: Lamplight Nook runs the official installer in the background; no windows open.
setup.claudeInstallFailed: That didn't work. You can install it yourself with the steps below.
setup.claudeOld: Claude Code on this computer is {version}, older than the {tested} the shop has tried. Some jobs may stop partway.
setup.claudeUpdateFailed: That didn't work. You can update it yourself with the steps below: it's the same line as installing.
setup.keyStep1: Sign in to the Anthropic Console, or sign up if you don't have an account.
setup.keyStep2: Add credit under Billing first, at least $5. A key won't work without it.
setup.keyStep3: Under API Keys, create a key, copy it and paste it below.
setup.keyMissing: No API key yet. Paste it below. It's stored encrypted on this computer only.
setup.keyStored: API key saved ({hint}), on this computer only.
setup.keyFromEnv: Using the key in the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable ({hint}).
setup.keySubscription: Developer mode: using the signed-in Claude subscription.
setup.keyUnverified: Can't reach Anthropic right now. Saved anyway; we'll know if it works on the first job.
setup.keyBadFormat: That doesn't look like an API key. It should start with sk-ant-.
setup.keyInvalid: Anthropic says this key doesn't work. Check it was copied in full, or try another.
setup.keyNoStorage: This computer can't store the key encrypted. You can use the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable instead.
setup.laterHint: Not ready? That's fine, come in anyway. Click the counter to watch a trial run.
setup.folderText: Each commission gets its own folder here, with everything that was made.
setup.greetHint: Need something? Write it on the slip at the counter.
setup.readyText: Claude Code and your API key are ready. Write what you need on the commission slip and hand it to Wick.
setup.trialOffer: Want to see how the shop usually works first?
setup.trialEndText: That was a recorded sample: the staff took an "expense tracker" commission. Install Claude Code and add an API key, and you can hand in your own.
setup.lookHint: This is how you'll look when you drop by with a commission.
setup.spendMonth: About {cost} this month. This is Claude Code's estimate. It reports no cost for a stretch stopped partway, so the shop estimates that from what was used. Anthropic's bill is what counts.
setup.budgetHint: At the limit the staff stop and wait for you to say carry on.
setup.monthCapHint: At the limit, new work waits. Wick says so before it gets there.
setup.troubleText: Export a diagnostics file and send it to us. It holds only the app's log and an outline of your computer and settings: no API key, nothing from your commissions.
setup.troubleDone: Saved, and selected in its folder for you.
setup.writeText: Or write to us. Lamplight Nook sends nothing itself: it opens the mail program on your computer with the lines below filled in. The rest is yours to write, and sending is up to you.
setup.writeBody: Body: yours to write; the last line names the app version and system, like {footer}
setup.writeDiag: Export the diagnostics file too (drag it into the letter yourself afterwards)
setup.writeOpened: Your mail program is open. What to write, and whether to send it, is up to you.
setup.writeOpenedDiag: Your mail program is open, and the diagnostics file is selected in its folder: drag it into the letter. Sending is up to you.
setup.writeFailed: Your mail program didn't open. You can write to {email} directly.
setup.mailPrompt: (Write what happened here: what you did, and what you saw.)
setup.mailDiag: Diagnostics: {file} (please drag it into this letter)
setup.claudeStoreHint: Three steps below, once. This row turns green by itself when it's done.
setup.claudeStoreUpdate: Three steps below, once (it's the same line as installing). This row turns green by itself when it's done.
setup.reportSubject: Lamplight Nook {version}: about something the staff made
setup.reportPrompt: (Write what wasn't right: what the staff said or made.)
setup.languageRestart: The new language takes effect when Lamplight Nook restarts.
setup.legalText: Lamplight Nook collects no data; commissions go to Anthropic only through your own Claude Code.
setup.legalLine: By opening the shop you agree to the
setup.noticesMissing: The license list is missing. Reinstalling Lamplight Nook should bring it back.
setup.updatesToggle: Have Pip bring word of new versions
setup.updatesHint: It only looks. Nothing downloads until you press Update.
setup.creditArt: Pixel art for the shop and characters: LimeZu, Modern Interiors, Modern Exteriors and Modern Farm
setup.creditFont: Handwriting font: LXGW WenKai (SIL Open Font License 1.1)
setup.volumeHint: For some quiet, click the little speaker at the top left.
setup.creditSound: Interface sounds: Andrea Baroni (Cyberleaf Studio), Modern UI SFX. The door bell, mallet and pencil sounds are made by Lamplight Nook itself
setup.creditMusic: Background music: Alex Morgan, Jazz Study Sessions and Jazz Cafe & Coffee Shop (CC BY 4.0; converted to Ogg and evened out in volume)

door.leaves: Another layer of leaves on the step.

guest.baker: Fresh from the oven. Eat it while it's hot.

guest.student: I'll only sit a while. Don't mind me.

objects.you: Your commission is under way. Have a seat.

grownMade.album: We made an album once, so one stays here to leaf through.
grownMade.calendar: We planned a schedule, and the calendar went up.
grownMade.books: After two rounds of research, the books stayed.
grownMade.letters: We wrote a few letters. The replies get pinned here.
grownMade.ledger: After a couple of sheets we keep our own books better.
grownMade.monitor: After a few web pages, this little computer stays on.
grownMade.briefcase: We wrote someone a résumé, and this briefcase stayed.
grownMade.readinglamp: We made some reading notes, and a reading lamp went on the table.
grownMade.postcards: We made a travel guide, and postcards went up on the wall.
grownMade.toolbox: We made a small tool, and Flint brought his toolbox over.

run.cancelConfirm: Call it off? Files already made will stay.
run.progressThinking: Wick is working out the plan
run.progressGuess: Wick's rough guess, not a real plan yet
run.queued: “{title}” is in the queue: it starts once the work ahead of it is done.
run.queuedMoney: “{title}” waits in the queue: there is not enough left under the cap to start it yet.
run.firstHint: Ring the bell if you have more to say. The plan goes on the blackboard.
run.netTitle: Looks like the internet is down
run.netText: Tried a few times and couldn't reach Anthropic. Carry on once you're back online; nothing done so far is lost.
run.busyText: Anthropic's service is too busy right now, or requests are being rate limited. Try again in a few minutes.
run.billingText: This API key has run out of credit or hit its limit. Check billing in Anthropic's console, top up, then carry on.
run.authText: This API key is invalid or expired. Put in a new one under "Ready to work?" in Settings.
run.budgetText: This round has spent about {cost}, the per-round limit you set. Carrying on allows the same again; or raise the limit in Settings first.
run.monthCapText: About {spent} has gone this month, of the {cap} monthly limit. What is left is not enough for another round. Raise the limit in Settings, or wait for next month.
run.projectCapText: "{project}" has cost about {spent}, of its {cap} limit. What is left is not enough for another round. You can raise the project's limit in the notebook.
run.monthCapNewsText: From this version, each month has a spending limit too. One of the last few months went over {default}, so it starts at {cap} and the update won't stop you straight away. Change it any time in Settings.
run.pendingText: "{want}" stopped halfway. Carry on with it?
run.interruptedText: These were under way when the computer shut down. Each kept its place, so carrying on won't start over.
run.closeText: If you close now the staff will stop. You can carry on next time you open Lamplight Nook.
run.failedText: The work stopped partway through, and I can't say why. What's done so far is safe, and you can carry on.
run.goneText: It may have been moved or deleted. If you still want it, hand in a new commission.
run.tooBigText: It now holds over 100 MB, more than the shop can keep a copy of, so an undo couldn't be promised and the work hasn't started. Move some big files out, then hand it in again.

access.captionsToggle: Always show the latest line at the bottom

access.detailedToggle: Show what the staff are doing at the bottom of the window
access.hotspotBell: Meeting bell: call everyone to the big table
access.hotspotGarden: Back door: look out at the garden
access.hotspotHens: The hens: toss them some grain
access.bedsBare: Vegetable beds: empty until the first job is done
access.bedsRest: {n} resting under straw for the winter
access.hotspotBoard: The blackboard: the whole plan, or the project board when nothing is under way
access.hotspotWorks: The works shelf: see what we made together

connections.title: Connections
connections.intro: Once connected, the staff may use these things from outside the shop. Tick which ones a commission may use on its slip; unticked, they stay out.
connections.storage: This computer can't lock its key away safely, so it was not connected.
connections.allPaused: All connections are paused in settings, so the slip does not list them for now.
connections.pauseAllHint: While on, the slip lists no connections, and a commission under way is refused the next time it uses one.

test.label: Test connection
test.readNote: read the note in the test connection
test.saveNote: save a note in the test folder
test.saveNoteUndo: Yes. Press Undo on the Outside actions page of the notebook, and the saved note is deleted.

reads: a test note that comes with the development build

does.what: show the note to the staff
save a note in the test folder, asking you every time

never: touch any other file on your computer
grant.disconnect: Press Disconnect on the Connections page of the notebook. The note and its key are deleted; the record of what it did stays.

actions.title: Outside actions
actions.intro: Everything the staff did through a connection: what it was, whether you agreed, and whether it worked. What was read or written is not kept.
actions.given: agreed by the tick on the slip
actions.undoFailed: It can't be undone now; what it made may already be gone.

notebook.ledgerWorks: This month: {works} commissions, {rounds} rounds, {time} a round on average.
notebook.ledgerConsults: Talks with Wick before a commission: {n}, about {cost} of that.
notebook.ledgerWaits: Errands waited their turn {n} times, {time} in all.
notebook.ledgerSince: Kept since {date}, on this computer only. None of it is sent anywhere.
notebook.ledgerCleared: Cleared. Every commission is still here.
notebook.sectionText: Wick notes down past commissions, the choices you made and where things got stuck. Only that, never your conversations.
notebook.title: Wick's notebook
notebook.troubleTitle: Some of the shop's records can't be read
notebook.troubleRestored: That's rare. I filled the notebook in from the copy I made when the shop last opened, so anything since then may be missing. Everything we made is still in its folder.
notebook.troubleMissing: The notebook has gone missing. I filled it in from the copy I made when the shop last opened, so anything since then may be missing. Everything we made is still in its folder.
notebook.troubleSettings: The settings can't be read, so they're back to how they started. The most to spend per round is now ${budget}, and the work folder and language are back to their defaults too. Have a look in Settings.
notebook.troubleLedger: The spending ledger can't be read, so what was spent before is no longer in it. Your bill with Anthropic isn't affected.
notebook.troubleKept: The files that can't be read are still in the data folder, with broken in their names.
notebook.troubleLost: That's rare, and there's no good copy of the notebook to hand, so I've started a new one. Everything we made is still in its folder.
notebook.forgetBusy: Not while a commission is running. Whatever it's doing would go straight back in the notebook. Try again once it's finished.
notebook.forgetConfirm: Really forget everything? It can't be brought back, and what the shop gathered gets packed away too. What each month cost stays, but no longer says which commission it went on. Claude Code's own records, in its .claude folder, stay too.
notebook.forgotten: OK, it's all crossed out. Your name is still in Settings; change it any time.
notebook.metLine: {name} came by for the first time
notebook.bedSprout: the first vegetable went in out back
notebook.bedRipe: the first vegetable out back was ripe
notebook.bedFull: the beds out back filled up
notebook.apprentice: Bean came to the shop as an apprentice

tray.notifyToggle: Show a notification when work finishes, stops or needs you
tray.closeToTrayToggle: Closing the window keeps the shop open in the tray
tray.tooltipWaiting: Lamplight Nook: waiting for your decision
tray.openAtLoginToggle: Open Lamplight Nook in the tray when the computer starts
tray.doneBody: Click to see what was made.
tray.budgetBody: Click to decide whether to carry on.
tray.skippedBody: Not enough budget left. It will try again next time.

meeting.title: A quick meeting
meeting.text: Anything to add or change? Everyone's listening.
meeting.placeholder: e.g. add a total for the month too
meeting.projectText: Anything to add or change on “{title}”? This crew is listening.

revise.title: Change it a bit
revise.text: What's not quite right? Tell us and we'll work from this version.
revise.placeholder: e.g. a lighter colour, bigger buttons
revise.keep: We'll keep a copy of this version first, so you can go back to it.

ui.resultReport: Something not right in this? Tell us
ui.resultPreview: A preview of {file}. Click to open it.

resultNotOpened.macros: This file carries macros, which run as soon as it opens, so it is shown in its folder instead. Open it yourself only if you trust it.
resultNotOpened.embedded: This file has an embedded object or control that could run when it opens, so it is shown in its folder instead.
resultNotOpened.externalTemplate: This file fetches a template from elsewhere when it opens, so it is shown in its folder instead.
resultNotOpened.externalLink: This file links to files or addresses outside it and would fetch them when it opens, so it is shown in its folder instead.
resultNotOpened.unreadable: This file can't be read and may be damaged, so it is shown in its folder instead.

citations.title: Sources
citations.more: {n} sources in all; the first {shown} are listed.
citations.unnumbered: Key points with no source number: {n}.
citations.missing: The summary cites {numbers}, which the source list does not have.
citations.noSources: This research came without its list of sources (sources.json), so they can't be checked.
citations.unreadable: The list of sources (sources.json) can't be read, so they can't be checked.

resultConverted.pdfToWord: A PDF can't be changed as it is, so the changed version is a Word document.
resultConverted.sheetAsList: This workbook has charts, pivot tables, tables or links that changing its cells could break, so it was left as it was. The changes are written down as a list for you to make.

ui.resultShelf: Finished work goes on the shelf by the wall. Click it any time to find this again or change it.
ui.resultScriptDeletes: {file} has a command that deletes files. Read it before you run it, or use "Change it a bit" to have it taken out.
ui.resultScriptNoPreview: {file} changes files as soon as it runs, without listing what it will do first. Read it before you run it.
ui.resultScriptBoth: {file} deletes files, and does it as soon as it runs, without listing what it will do first. Read it before you run it, or use "Change it a bit" to have it fixed.
ui.resultRestore: Go back to the last version
ui.resultRestoreBack: Go back to the changed version
ui.resultRestored: Done, this is the last version again.
ui.resultRestoredBack: Done, this is the changed version again.
ui.resultRestoreFailed: Couldn't switch; the folder may have been moved.

projects.title: The project board
projects.text: One row per project. Open one to see each of its rounds.
projects.empty: No projects yet. The first commission we finish starts one.
projects.waitProject: Waiting for this project's round under way
projects.waitMoney: Waiting for money: not enough left under the cap

schedule.title: Do regularly: {title}
schedule.text: When the time comes, the shop takes the commission itself and carries on in this project. The shop has to be open, in the tray is fine.
schedule.wantPlaceholder: For example: put this week's numbers into a weekly report
schedule.past: That time has already gone by.
schedule.empty: Say what to do each time.
schedule.missed: Missed the one at {at}, not made up
schedule.closedNote: Scheduled commissions don't run while the shop is closed.
schedule.paused: Scheduled commissions are paused. Switch them back on from the tray menu.

projects.opened: That opened a copy; the project’s folder is untouched.
projects.revertAsk: What is there now is kept as a version first, then round {n} comes back.
projects.reverted: Back to round {n}. The timeline has one more round.
projects.forked: Branched off: the new project is “{title}”. The old one is untouched.
projects.failed: That didn’t work. The folder may be gone, or the shop is at work.
projects.none: No version was kept of this round.
projects.goneRounds: The versions of rounds {list} are gone. When a project’s versions pass 200 MB, the oldest go, all but round 1.
projects.lent: This is your own folder, lent to the shop, so it can’t be branched off: that would copy all of it.

brief.title: What the staff remember
brief.text: The staff read this before every round. What you change here stays as you wrote it.
brief.lastRound: Where the last round left off
brief.prefLimit: Up to {n}, of up to {chars} characters each.
brief.saved: Saved. The next round goes by this.
brief.forgetAsk: The staff will forget all of this, and the next round won't pick up the last conversation. The timeline and the files stay.
brief.forgot: Forgotten. The next round starts by looking at the folder afresh.

shelf.title: The works shelf
shelf.text: Everything we've made together ends up here.
shelf.gone: Can't find it; it may have been moved or deleted.
shelf.relinkWrong: The main file isn't in that folder.
shelf.relinkBroad: That folder holds a lot more than this work. Give it a folder of its own and show me that one.
shelf.relinkTaken: Another work is already there. Give this one a folder of its own and show me that one.
shelf.relinked: Found it. It opens from there now.
shelf.taken: Saved. It's picked out for you in its folder.
shelf.takeEmpty: Nothing of this work is left in the folder to take.
shelf.empty: The shelf is still empty. The first thing we finish goes right here.
shelf.search: Find one: a name, what you asked, a month
shelf.noMatch: Nothing matches. Try other words, or another kind.

mini.toggle: Keep a small window in the corner while the shop is out of sight
mini.title: Lamplight Nook mini
mini.idle: Quiet in the shop. Tea time.
mini.waiting: Wick needs your call. Click to go back in.
mini.serious: ⚠ A step needs your OK. Click to go back in.
mini.done: All done. Click to have a look.
mini.failed: Didn't work out. Click to go back in.

moveIn.title: Bring your shop over?
moveIn.found: Wick found the Lamplight Nook you installed from the website on this computer: {works} finished works, with {spent} in the ledger.
moveIn.text: Bring it over and your works, the notebook and the ledger carry on here. The original stays where it is, and the other version still opens. Your API key can't come along: paste it in Settings again afterwards.
moveIn.failed: Couldn't bring it over. The original hasn't been touched.

update.postman: Letter for the Nook. From the makers.
update.title: Lamplight Nook {version} is out
update.intro: Pip brought a letter: there's a new version of Lamplight Nook. Press Update to fetch it now. It goes in when you close the shop, so nothing you've asked for gets cut short, and your data is backed up first.
update.fetching: Right, I'll go and fetch it.
update.ready: Got the new version. It goes in when you close up.
update.failed: Couldn't fetch it. Pip will bring word again.

scene.label: Where the shop is

privacy: Lamplight Nook collects none of your data: no analytics, no ads, nothing reported in the background. We run no servers and cannot see what happens in your shop.

Your name and settings; your API key, encrypted with the system's own encryption so only you on this computer can unlock it; Wick's notebook (past commissions, the choices you made, where things got stuck); an estimate of what each month cost; records of the last 50 commissions; the last 7 days of the app's log; crash records.

All of this is in the app's data folder (on Windows, %APPDATA%\Lamplight Nook; the Microsoft Store version keeps it in the app's own storage, which Windows removes when you uninstall). You can clear everything the shop remembers from Wick's notebook. Claude Code also keeps its own record of each job, in the .claude folder in your home folder; those belong to Claude Code and stay when you do. If you installed from the setup file, delete that folder after uninstalling to remove everything.
What the staff make goes in the commission folder you chose, and it is yours.

The staff work through Claude Code on your computer. Your commissions, anything you add in a meeting, the contents of files the staff read in the commission folder, and web searches are sent to Anthropic through Claude Code with your own API key. Anthropic's privacy policy and commercial terms apply to that, and the cost goes to your own Anthropic account.
When you save an API key, Lamplight Nook makes one free request to Anthropic to check that it works.
Other than that, Lamplight Nook connects to no servers. When the staff look things up they visit the web pages they find.

A diagnostics file leaves your computer only when you export it in Settings and send it to us yourself. It holds the app's log and an outline of your computer and settings, with no API key and nothing from your commissions.
For questions, use the support contact on Lamplight Nook's Microsoft Store page. If this note changes, it is updated with a new version and the date above changes.
